texts.consent_body: This survey is part of a graduate class project for an Affective Computing course at Northeastern University. It is not published research. You will describe a recent setback with a lifestyle goal, read four short messages written by AI, and answer questions about them. It takes about 15–20 minutes. Participation is voluntary, and you can stop at any time by closing the page. We do not collect your name or email. Your responses will be used only for this class project and deleted when the course ends. Some questions ask about difficult feelings after a setback; you can skip any optional question you are not comfortable answering. The setback description is needed to write your messages. Questions: [team contact email].
texts.declined: You chose not to take part. Thank you for your time. You can close this window.
texts.screened_out: Thank you for your interest. Based on your answers, this study is not a good fit for you right now. We appreciate your time. You can close this window.
texts.support_resources: Thank you for your time. If you are struggling with eating, exercise, or how you feel about yourself, please reach out to someone you trust or a health professional. In the US, you can call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) or text HOME to 741741 (Crisis Text Line), any time. Outside the US, please contact your local health or crisis services.
texts.generating: Preparing your messages. This usually takes 10-30 seconds. Please don't close this window.
texts.generation_error: Sorry, something went wrong while preparing your messages. Please try again in a moment. If this keeps happening, contact the project team.
texts.f_instruction: Imagine your AI coach sent you this message right after the setback you described. Read it, then answer the questions.
texts.compare_instruction: Here are the four messages you read about your setback.
texts.debrief: Thank you. In this study the four messages were written by AI in four styles: neutral, strict, generally encouraging, and encouraging in a way tailored to how you described your setback. We are studying which style best helps people keep going after a slip. Setbacks are a normal part of any lifestyle change. If this study brought up difficult feelings about eating, exercise or yourself, please reach out to someone you trust or a health professional. This was a class project, and your responses will be deleted when the course ends. Questions: [team contact email].
